title: Affineness, smoothness and connectedness in exact algebraic-group sequences
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $N,E,Q$ be separated group schemes of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $i:N\hookrightarrow E$ be a closed normal subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] and let $q:E\to Q$ be a homomorphism whose scheme-theoretic kernel is $i:N\hookrightarrow E$, meaning that the square with $N\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the identity section $e_Q:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Q$ is Cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose $q$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and surjective on underlying spaces. Thus $1\to N\to E\to Q\to1$ is an exact sequence of algebraic groups. Affine means isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring [def-pc-scheme], smoothness means [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and connected means [def-weil-connected-scheme]. For each of the three properties affine, smooth, and connected, the following hold separately: if $N$ and $Q$ have the property, then $E$ has it; if $E$ has the property, then $Q$ has it. Neither commutativity nor perfectness of $k$ is assumed, and the trivial group is allowed.

source.place: Proposition 8.1(a),(b), printed p.149. Its cited inputs are Proposition 1.62 (smoothness), printed p.24; Corollary 2.70 (affine extensions), printed p.61; Proposition 5.29 (affine quotients), printed p.105; Proposition 5.59 (connectedness), printed p.114. Exactness is defined in Section 1(e), printed pp.23--24. No single Stacks tag states this algebraic-group permanence theorem.

proof.text: First establish the finiteness needed for descent. The field $k$ is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian. By [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], $Q$ is locally Noetherian. By clause (f) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], $q$ is locally of finite type, because $E\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is. Hence [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $q$ locally of finite presentation. Both $E$ and $Q$ are quasi-compact, and $Q$ is quasi-separated: its diagonal is a closed immersion, hence affine by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc], hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $q$ quasi-compact. Its flatness and surjectivity are hypotheses. In particular $\{q:E\to Q\}$ is an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: for an affine open $V\subset Q$, cover the quasi-compact inverse image $q^{-1}(V)$ by finitely many affine opens; their images cover $V$.

source.place: Definition 1.61, p.24; finite-type refinement using Stacks 01T6, 01T8, 01TX; singleton fpqc condition, Stacks 022B.

proof.text:
The kernel square and the group operations [def-sc-group-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product] give inverse scheme morphisms
$$\alpha:E\times_kN\longrightarrow E\times_QE,\quad(g,n)\longmapsto(g,g\,i(n)),\qquad
\beta:(g,h)\longmapsto(g,g^{-1}h).$$
For $\beta$, the second component factors uniquely through $N$, since $q(g)^{-1}q(h)=e_Q$. The two composites are identities by $g^{-1}(g\,i(n))=i(n)$ and $g(g^{-1}h)=h$, using uniqueness in the fibre-product universal property. Both maps preserve the first projection to $E$. These are formulas in morphisms, using multiplication and inverse, so they hold after every base change, including nonreduced test schemes.

source.place: Example 2.68 and Exercise 2-1, pp.60--61; Proposition 5.24, pp.104--105.

proof.text: Assume $N$ and $Q$ affine. The structure map $N\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine by [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Its base change $E\times_kN\to E$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1). Step 2 identifies this projection with the base change of $q$ along itself. Since step 1 gives the fpqc cover $\{q\}$, [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-affine] makes $q$ affine. Its target $Q$ is affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](2) makes $E$ affine.

Assume $E$ affine. The closed immersion $N\hookrightarrow E$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc], and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](2) makes $N$ affine. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] to the normal closed subgroup $N\subset E$, obtaining an affine finite-type group $Q_0$ and a flat surjective finitely presented homomorphism $q_0:E\to Q_0$ with kernel $N$. The same argument as step 1 makes $\{q_0\}$ an fpqc cover. By step 2, both relations $E\times_QE$ and $E\times_{Q_0}E$ consist of pairs $(g,gi(n))$. Therefore $q_0$ agrees on the two projections of $E\times_QE$, and $q$ agrees on those of $E\times_{Q_0}E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], $q_0$ descends along $q$ to $a:Q\to Q_0$, and $q$ descends along $q_0$ to $b:Q_0\to Q$. They satisfy $aq=q_0$ and $bq_0=q$. Consequently $ba$ and $\mathrm{id}_Q$ have the same pullback along $q$, and $ab$ and $\mathrm{id}_{Q_0}$ have the same pullback along $q_0$. The uniqueness clause of that descent theorem gives $ba=\mathrm{id}_Q$ and $ab=\mathrm{id}_{Q_0}$. Hence $Q\simeq Q_0$ is affine.

source.place: Proposition 5.29 and its proof using quotient uniqueness Theorem 5.13, pp.101,105; Stacks 023Q, representable fpqc descent.

proof.text: Assume $N$ and $Q$ smooth over $k$. By [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), the projection $E\times_kN\to E$ is smooth. Step 2 identifies it with $E\times_QE\to E$, the pullback of $q$ along $q$. The flat quasi-compact surjection $q$ of step 1 therefore permits [lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent] to conclude that $q$ is smooth. Composing it with the smooth structure map of $Q$ by [lem-trf-smooth-composition] proves that $E$ is smooth.

source.place: Proposition 1.62(a), p.24, with the torsor computation of 2.68; Stacks 01VB, 02VL, 01VA.

proof.text: Assume $E$ smooth over $k$. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] to $E\xrightarrow{q}Q\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its hypotheses on $q$ are flatness and surjectivity from the statement and local finite presentation from step 1; the composite is the smooth structure map of $E$. Thus $Q$ is smooth. This argument does not require the kernel to be smooth.

source.place: Proposition 1.62(b), p.24, in its smooth source-descent form, Stacks 05B5 (lemma-smooth-permanence).

proof.text: Assume $N$ connected. Its identity is a $k$-rational point, so [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] gives connectedness of $N_L$ for every field extension $L/k$. For $y\in Q$, let $F=E\times_Q\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. The homeomorphism in that definition and surjectivity of $q$ make $F$ nonempty. Choose any point $x\in F$ and put $L=\kappa(x)$; the canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to F$ gives an $L$-point $g$ of $F_L$. Translation $n\mapsto g\,i(n)$ identifies $N_L$ with $F_L$, with inverse $h\mapsto g^{-1}h$, exactly by the kernel calculation in step 2. The map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ is surjective (both spectra have one point); its base change $F_L\to F$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Thus $F$ is connected: a nonempty clopen separation would pull back to one of the connected space $N_L$. The homeomorphism of [def-pc-scheme-fibre] now shows that every topological fibre $q^{-1}(y)$ is connected.

source.place: Proposition 5.59(a), p.114, via the torsor fibre calculation of 2.68; Stacks 04KV, 01S1, 01K1.

proof.text: If also $Q$ is connected, step 7 gives connected nonempty fibres of $q$. Step 1 gives flatness, quasi-compactness and surjectivity, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-qc-surjective-quotient-map] says that $Q$ has the quotient topology for $q$. Taking the whole closed connected subset $Q$ in [lem-weil-pbc-connected-fibres-quotient-preimage-connected] proves that $E$ is connected.

Finally suppose $E$ connected. If $Q=U\amalg V$ were a separation into nonempty clopen subsets, then $E=q^{-1}(U)\amalg q^{-1}(V)$ would be a separation into nonempty clopen subsets by continuity and surjectivity. This contradicts connectedness of $E$ [def-weil-connected-scheme]. The identity section makes $Q$ nonempty. Hence $Q$ is connected, completing all six implications. No inference asserts any of these properties for $N$ from the corresponding property of $E$.

No new nodes and no statement change.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q61-2aabaa14e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item split. It has 9 steps and no new nodes. Diffing against clones/live shows the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged. The statement matches Milne iAG Prop 8.1(a),(b) on p.149: an exact sequence where the kernel is a Cartesian square and q is flat and surjective, for separated finite-type groups over a field. Nothing is weakened. Step 1: q is locally of finite type by cancellation and then locally of finite presentation, since k is Noetherian. Q is quasi-separated because its diagonal is a closed immersion, hence affine, hence quasi-compact; that makes q quasi-compact, and {q} is an fpqc covering checked straight from the definition. Step 2: the torsor maps (g,n)->(g,g i(n)) and (g,h)->(g,g^{-1}h) are inverse; this was checked with the noncommutative order. Step 3: affineness descends along {q} (02L5), so E is affine over the affine Q. Step 4: E affine makes N affine. The affine-normal-quotient node gives Q0. Each of q and q0 kills the other's kernel pair, so representable fpqc descent (existence and uniqueness) gives a and b with ba=id and ab=id. This identifies the given Q with the constructed quotient rather than assuming it. Step 5: smooth base change, then smooth base descent along the flat quasi-compact surjection q (02VL), then composition. Step 6: smooth source descent (q flat, surjective, locally of finite presentation); it correctly assumes no smooth kernel, as the Frobenius on G_m with kernel mu_p requires. Step 7: N has a rational point, so N_L is connected for every L (04KV). Each fibre F is nonempty; a point x gives L=kappa(x) and an isomorphism N_L = F_L by translation. F_L -> F is surjective, so F is connected. No perfect field or closed point is needed. Step 8: flat quasi-compact surjections are quotient maps, and connected fibres then give connected E (0377). Step 9: a continuous surjective image of a connected space is connected, and e_Q makes Q nonempty. Small cases checked: trivial group, N=1, Q=1. Route: picard-rr, p1 and iff are on the unit route, and the lem-trf nodes are Mathlib leaves. I accept the declared tool_uses for 02L5, smooth source descent and 04KV as generic black boxes. No cycle, no SGA. lem-sfb-connected-group-extension covers only the algebraically closed affine connected case, so it is not a duplicate. Batch 5: lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent (02VL) and lem-trf-smooth-composition (01VA) are generic morphism facts, not steps of the trace formula or Poincare duality proofs. The route through affine-normal-quotient-geometry reaches only the general definition def-trf-scheme-cover-descent-datum. All three accepted. No changes.
